$meta.lookup: To find a type from a word: apply the trim step, then the lowercase step, then replace each run of spaces and '-' with one '_'. If a type has that exact name, use it; otherwise use the type whose aliases contain it; otherwise there is no match.

normalize_steps.lowercase: Unicode default lowercase mapping, locale-independent: the full mapping, so U+0130 becomes i + U+0307 and a final capital sigma becomes U+03C2. In Go use golang.org/x/text/cases, not strings.ToLower.
normalize_steps.trim: Remove leading and trailing Unicode White_Space: U+0009-U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000.
normalize_steps.uppercase: Unicode default uppercase mapping, locale-independent: the full mapping, so U+00DF becomes SS. In Go use golang.org/x/text/cases, not strings.ToUpper.

fractional_seconds.description: Fractional-second digits kept; values beyond it are rounded. Postgres: time(p), timestamp(p), timestamptz(p), interval(p).

length.description: Most characters a value may have; omitted means unlimited. HTML: maxlength. Postgres: varchar(n).

nullable.description: Whether the field accepts null. Applies to every type, so no type lists it. Postgres: false emits NOT NULL.

precision.description: Total significant digits; omitted means unlimited. Postgres: numeric(precision, scale).

scale.description: Digits kept right of the decimal point; requires precision. Negative rounds left of the point. Postgres: numeric(precision, scale).

values.description: The allowed values, in order; the order is also the sort order. HTML: the select options. Postgres: CREATE TYPE ... AS ENUM (...); values can be added later, never removed.

collation.description: Collation driving comparison and ordering; defaults to the database collation. Applies to every text and varchar column, so no type lists it.

fields.description: Restricts which units are stored; omitted keeps every field.

name.description: Name of the generated enum type, unique per schema.

any.details: Deliberately unconstrained: passthrough payloads and escape hatches. Reach for it last - every consumer inherits the validation burden.

html.note: No native JSON input; parse with JSON.parse before submit or use a structured editor.

any.label: Anything
any.name: any

array.details: An ordered JSON list: tags, attachments, embedded collections. Prefer a separate table or repeated field when elements need identity or independent querying.
array.error: Please give a list of values.

html.note: No native JSON input; parse with JSON.parse before submit or use a structured editor.

array.label: List
array.name: array

postgres.note: A native array (text[]) is the alternative when every element shares one scalar type.

base64.details: Binary content as standard base64 text: payloads embedded in JSON. Prefer binary for raw transport and base64url when the value travels in URLs or filenames.
base64.error: Please use base64 with = padding, like SGVsbG8gd29ybGQ=.

html.note: Read the file and encode it (FileReader.readAsDataURL, then strip the data: prefix).

base64.label: Base64 data
base64.name: base64

postgres.note: Stored decoded, not as the base64 text; bytea_output picks hex or escape on the way out.

base64url.details: URL-safe base64 (no + or /): tokens and digests placed in URLs. Prefer base64 for ordinary embedded payloads.
base64url.error: Please use letters, digits, - and _, like SGVsbG8gd29ybGQ.

html.note: Encode as base64, then replace + with -, / with _ and drop padding.

base64url.label: URL-safe base64
base64url.name: base64url

postgres.note: Same bytes as base64; only the transport alphabet differs.

bic.details: A BIC/SWIFT code identifying a bank for payment routing. Routing, not identity - prefer lei to identify the legal entity itself.
bic.error: Please use 8 or 11 capital letters and digits, like DEUTDEFF500.

attrs.title: Please use 8 or 11 capital letters and digits, like DEUTDEFF500.

bic.label: Bank code (BIC)
bic.name: bic

binary.details: Raw bytes: file uploads, blobs, digests. Inside JSON they travel as standard base64 (RFC 4648); storage keeps the decoded bytes.

html.note: Encode the file's bytes to base64 for JSON, or send multipart/form-data and skip the encoding.

binary.label: File
binary.name: binary

postgres.note: Variable length with no fixed-size form; large payloads can move to a large object instead.

binary.standard: OpenAPI 3.2 binary data / RFC 4648 Section 4 (base64 in JSON)

boolean.details: A true/false fact: flags, toggles, switches. Prefer enum if a third state could ever appear, rather than a nullable boolean.

html.note: An unchecked box submits nothing; map absence to false.

boolean.label: Yes or no
boolean.name: boolean

char.details: Exactly one character: a grade, flag, or single-letter code. Prefer string for anything that can grow, and enum when the values form a closed set.
char.error: Please type exactly one character, like A.
char.label: Single character
char.name: char

postgres.note: Bare char is char(1); the blank-padding that makes char awkward needs a length above 1.

cidr.details: A network prefix of either IP family: allowlists, routing rules. Prefer ipv4 or ipv6 for a single host.
cidr.error: Please use an address, a slash and a size, like 192.0.2.0/24.
cidr.hint: An address and a size, like 192.0.2.0/24
cidr.label: Network range
cidr.name: cidr

postgres.note: Rejects any bit set to the right of the netmask, which inet accepts.

color.details: An sRGB color as lowercase #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa - the exact form <input type="color"> produces, so it round-trips through forms, JSON, JS/TS and SQL unchanged. Prefer css_color only for wide-gamut or design-token values.
color.error: Please use # and 6 small hex digits, like #1a2b3c.

html.note: The picker returns lowercase #rrggbb; #rrggbbaa needs the newer alpha attribute where supported, else a separate opacity input.

color.label: Color
color.name: color
color.standard: CSS Color Module Level 4 (hex notation), canonical lowercase

commonmark.details: Markdown (CommonMark) source: user-authored rich content stored as written. Prefer html for already-rendered markup and text for plain prose.

html.note: Pair with a rendered preview; sanitize the rendered HTML.

commonmark.label: Markdown
commonmark.name: commonmark

postgres.note: Markdown source; Postgres stores the text and never parses it.

country.details: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (US): the interchange default for countries.
country.error: Please use the 2-letter country code, like US.
country.label: Country
country.name: country

postgres.note: char(2) fits but blank-pads and compares by the padded value; text avoids that.

country_alpha3.details: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (USA): feeds and standards that require three letters. Prefer country (alpha-2) as the default.
country_alpha3.error: Please use the 3-letter country code, like USA.

html.note: Intl has no alpha-3 list; map from alpha-2 with a lookup table.

country_alpha3.label: Country (3-letter)
country_alpha3.name: country_alpha3

cron.details: A POSIX crontab expression (0 3 * * *): recurring schedules. Prefer duration for simple intervals and date_time for one-shot schedules.
cron.error: Please use five fields, like 0 3 * * * (3 AM daily).
cron.label: Schedule
cron.name: cron

css_color.details: Any single CSS Color 4 value: hex, named, rgb(), hsl(), hwb(), lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch() or color(display-p3 ...). The pattern only checks the shape; validate for real with CSS.supports('color', value). Level 5 expressions (color-mix(), relative colors, light-dark(), var()) are computed in context and are deliberately not data.
css_color.error: That doesn't look like a CSS color. Try oklch(70% 0.15 250).

attrs.title: That doesn't look like a CSS color. Try oklch(70% 0.15 250).

html.note: Validate with CSS.supports('color', value); pair with <input type="color"> only when the value is sRGB hex.

css_color.label: CSS color
css_color.name: css_color

currency.details: An ISO 4217 currency code (USD): pair it with a decimal amount to represent money. Never derive it from country or locale - people transact across borders.
currency.error: Please use the 3-letter currency code, like USD.
currency.hint: Pick a currency, like USD or EUR
currency.label: Currency
currency.name: currency

date.details: A calendar date with no time or zone: birthdays, due dates, effective dates. Prefer date_time for an actual instant.
date.label: Date
date.name: date

date_time.details: An absolute instant with offset - the default for created/updated timestamps and anything that really happened. Prefer date_time_local only for deliberately floating times.
date_time.error: Please use date, T, time and zone, like 2026-08-16T14:30:00Z.
date_time.hint: An exact moment, with its time zone

html.note: No native input for an instant. datetime-local yields a wall-clock time; combine it with the user's zone (Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone) and convert to an offset or Z before sending.

date_time.label: Date and time
date_time.name: date_time

postgres.note: Stored as UTC and rendered in the session TimeZone; timestamp keeps no offset at all.

date_time_local.details: A date and time with no offset: floating events like 'Jan 1 at midnight, wherever the user is'. Prefer date_time for real instants; pair with timezone to reconstruct one.
date_time_local.error: Please use date, T and time, like 2026-08-16T14:30:00.
date_time_local.hint: A date and time on the clock, no zone

html.note: Exact match; browsers submit HH:MM without seconds unless step is set - append ":00" if absent.

date_time_local.label: Local date and time
date_time_local.name: date_time_local

postgres.note: timestamp keeps no offset at all; it names a wall clock, not an instant.

date_time_local.standard: OpenAPI Format Registry (RFC 3339 date-time with no offset)

decimal.details: Exact decimal value represented as text. Use for money, rates, quantities, and other values where decimal precision must be preserved. Precision and scale are determined by the target system.
decimal.error: Please use digits and one dot, like 1234.56.

attrs.title: Please use digits and one dot, like 1234.56.

html.note: Not type="number": that converts through a binary float. Keep it a string in JS; use a decimal library for math.

decimal.label: Exact number
decimal.name: decimal

postgres.note: Exact arithmetic. Without precision and scale it stores any value as given.

decimal128.details: IEEE 754 decimal128: exact decimals with a defined 34-significant-digit width, for interchange with fixed-width financial systems. Prefer decimal when arbitrary precision is acceptable.
decimal128.error: Please use digits and one dot, like 1234.567890123456789012345678901234.

attrs.title: Please use digits and one dot, like 1234.567890123456789012345678901234.

html.note: Not type="number": that converts through a binary float. Keep it a string in JS; use a decimal library for math.

decimal128.label: Very exact number
decimal128.name: decimal128

postgres.note: 34 significant decimal digits, which numeric holds exactly and a float does not.

doi.details: A Digital Object Identifier: citations to papers, datasets, publications. Prefer uri only for links that are not registered DOIs.

attrs.title: Please start with 10., like 10.1000/182.

doi.label: DOI
doi.name: doi

double_int.details: Integers exactly representable in an IEEE double (up to 2^53-1): safe as a plain number for every JSON consumer, including JavaScript. Prefer int64 when the full 64-bit range matters and consumers accept strings.
double_int.error: Please use a whole number between ±9007199254740991.
double_int.label: Safe whole number
double_int.name: double_int

postgres.note: Bounded by 2^53, so it always survives a round trip through a double.

double_int.standard: OpenAPI Format Registry (integer exactly representable as a double)

duration.details: A span of time (ISO 8601): timeouts, retention windows, billing periods. A length, not a position - prefer date_time for points in time.
duration.error: Please write it like P3DT4H30M (3 days, 4 hours, 30 minutes).
duration.hint: How long something lasts, like P3DT4H30M

attrs.title: Please write it like P3DT4H30M (3 days, 4 hours, 30 minutes).

html.note: No native duration input; usually rendered as separate number fields and assembled into ISO 8601.

duration.label: Length of time
duration.name: duration

postgres.note: Three independent components (months, days, microseconds) that never normalize into each other.

email.details: An email address: login and contact fields. Accepting internationalized mailboxes is a validation choice, not a separate type.
email.error: That email looks wrong. Try user@example.com.
email.label: Email address
email.name: email

postgres.note: The citext extension gives case-insensitive comparison without a lower() index.

enum.details: One value from a closed, named set: statuses, roles, kinds. Prefer string for open-ended sets and boolean for exactly two states.
enum.error: Please pick one of the options.
enum.hint: Pick one option from a fixed list

html.note: Options are the type's values; use radio buttons when there are few.

enum.label: Choice
enum.name: enum

postgres.note: Requires a named type created up front; Postgres rejects an inline unnamed enum.

float32.details: Single-precision floats: bulk sensor readings or ML weights where memory beats precision. Prefer float64 as the default floating-point type.
float32.label: Small-precision number
float32.name: float32

postgres.note: float(p) with p in 1-24 is a spelling of real; it is not a stored precision.

float64.details: The default floating-point number: measurements, ratios, scores. Never money or exact quantities - use decimal for anything where digits must be exact.
float64.label: Number
float64.name: float64

postgres.note: float(p) with p in 25-53 is a spelling of double precision.

gtin.details: A GS1 GTIN (UPC/EAN family) identifying a retail product. Prefer isbn when the domain is specifically books.

attrs.title: Please use 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits, like 0614141000036.

html.note: Usually scanned; the check digit needs code, not a pattern.

gtin.label: Barcode number
gtin.name: gtin

hostname.details: A DNS hostname: servers and endpoints without scheme or path. Prefer uri when a full locator travels; internationalized names are a validation choice.
hostname.error: Please use letters, digits, dots and dashes, like api.example.com.

attrs.title: Please use letters, digits, dots and dashes, like api.example.com.

hostname.label: Website name
hostname.name: hostname

html.details: HTML markup stored as-is: rendered output, email bodies. Sanitize on the way in; prefer commonmark when users author the content.

html.note: Sanitize (e.g. DOMPurify) before rendering; never assign untrusted input to innerHTML.

html.label: HTML
html.name: html

postgres.note: Markup source; escape it on output, not on the way in.

http_date.details: The HTTP header date format (IMF-fixdate): Last-Modified, Expires, and friends. HTTP interchange only - prefer date_time everywhere else.
http_date.error: Please use the HTTP date form, like Sun, 16 Aug 2026 14:30:00 GMT.

html.note: Not entered by people; format with new Date(value).toUTCString().

http_date.label: HTTP date
http_date.name: http_date

postgres.note: A header wire format, parsed to an instant on the way in. The OpenAPI registry still sources it to RFC 7231, which RFC 9110 obsoletes.

iban.details: An International Bank Account Number: identifying accounts for payments. Pair with bic for cross-border routing and treat as sensitive data.
iban.error: Please use capitals and digits, no spaces, like DE89370400440532013000.

attrs.title: Please use capitals and digits, no spaces, like DE89370400440532013000.

html.note: Users type it in groups of four; strip spaces and uppercase before submit, then verify the mod-97 checksum.

iban.label: Bank account (IBAN)
iban.name: iban

idn_email.details: An internationalized email address: non-ASCII local parts and domains. Prefer email when every consumer requires ASCII.
idn_email.error: That email looks wrong. Try ñoño@ejemplo.es.
idn_email.hint: Email that may use any alphabet

html.note: Not type="email": browsers reject non-ASCII local parts there.

idn_email.label: International email
idn_email.name: idn_email

idn_hostname.details: An internationalized (IDNA2008) hostname. Prefer hostname when values are guaranteed ASCII or already punycode-encoded.
idn_hostname.error: That domain looks wrong. Try bücher.example.
idn_hostname.label: International website name
idn_hostname.name: idn_hostname

int16.details: Signed 16-bit integers: compact numeric codes and small bounded quantities. Prefer int32 as the general-purpose default.
int16.error: Please use a whole number from -32768 to 32767.
int16.label: Small whole number
int16.name: int16

int32.details: The general-purpose signed integer: counts, quantities, offsets. Prefer int64 for identifiers or anything that can outgrow two billion.
int32.error: Please use a whole number, like 42.
int32.hint: A number with no decimal point, like 42
int32.label: Whole number
int32.name: int32

int64.details: Signed 64-bit integers: database keys, byte sizes, high-resolution counters. Values beyond 2^53 lose precision as JSON numbers, so they travel as strings; storage is still a native 64-bit integer.
int64.hint: A very big number with no decimal point

attrs.title: Please use only digits, like 9007199254740993.

html.note: Not type="number": browsers parse it as a double and lose digits past 2^53. Keep it a string in JS (BigInt for math).

int64.label: Big whole number
int64.name: int64

int8.details: Tiny signed integers (-128..127) where the bound is part of the contract. Prefer int32 as the general-purpose default.
int8.error: Please use a whole number from -128 to 127.
int8.label: Tiny whole number
int8.name: int8

postgres.note: Postgres has no 1-byte integer; smallint is the narrowest signed type.

ipv4.details: A dotted-quad IPv4 host address. Prefer cidr for networks rather than hosts.
ipv4.error: Please use four numbers from 0 to 255, like 192.0.2.1.

attrs.title: Please use four numbers from 0 to 255, like 192.0.2.1.

ipv4.label: IP address (v4)
ipv4.name: ipv4

postgres.note: inet holds a host with an optional netmask; use cidr when the value is a network.

ipv4_cidr.details: An IPv4 network prefix like 192.0.2.0/24. Prefer cidr when either family may appear, and ipv4 for a single host.
ipv4_cidr.error: Please use an IPv4 address, a slash and 0-32, like 192.0.2.0/24.

attrs.title: Please use an IPv4 address, a slash and 0-32, like 192.0.2.0/24.

ipv4_cidr.label: IPv4 network range
ipv4_cidr.name: ipv4_cidr

postgres.note: Rejects any bit set to the right of the netmask, which inet accepts.

ipv6.details: An IPv6 host address. Prefer cidr for prefixes rather than hosts.
ipv6.error: That IP address looks wrong. Try 2001:db8::1.
ipv6.label: IP address (v6)
ipv6.name: ipv6

postgres.note: One inet column stores both families; the address itself carries the version.

ipv6_cidr.details: An IPv6 network prefix like 2001:db8::/32. Prefer cidr when either family may appear, and ipv6 for a single host.
ipv6_cidr.error: Please use an IPv6 address, a slash and 0-128, like 2001:db8::/32.
ipv6_cidr.label: IPv6 network range
ipv6_cidr.name: ipv6_cidr

postgres.note: One cidr column stores both families; the prefix itself carries the version.

iri.details: An internationalized absolute URI: user-facing links in any script, unencoded. Prefer uri when consumers require ASCII with percent-encoding.
iri.error: That link looks wrong. Try https://bücher.example/straße.
iri.hint: A link that may use any alphabet

html.note: Not type="url": it normalizes non-ASCII to punycode/percent-encoding.

iri.label: International link
iri.name: iri

iri_reference.details: An internationalized URI reference, absolute or relative. Prefer iri for absolute-only values and uri_reference for ASCII-only ones.
iri_reference.error: That link or path looks wrong. Try ../straße.
iri_reference.hint: A link or path in any alphabet
iri_reference.label: International link or path
iri_reference.name: iri_reference

isbn.details: An ISBN identifying a book edition. Prefer gtin for general retail products; every ISBN-13 is a GTIN, but not the reverse.
isbn.error: Please use 10 or 13 digits, no dashes, like 9780306406157.

attrs.title: Please use 10 or 13 digits, no dashes, like 9780306406157.

html.note: Strip hyphens and spaces before submit; the check digit needs code, not a pattern.

isbn.label: Book number (ISBN)
isbn.name: isbn

json_pointer.details: An absolute JSON Pointer (/users/0/email): addressing a location inside a document from its root.
json_pointer.error: Start with / for each step, like /users/0/email.
json_pointer.hint: A path inside a document, like /users/0

attrs.title: Start with / for each step, like /users/0/email.

json_pointer.label: JSON Pointer
json_pointer.name: json_pointer

jwt.details: A compact JSON Web Token: signed claims passed between parties. Handle like secret in storage and logs; prefer secret for opaque credentials.
jwt.error: Please paste the whole token, like eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIn0.sig.

attrs.title: Please paste the whole token, like eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxIn0.sig.

jwt.label: Login token
jwt.name: jwt

language.details: An ISO 639 language code (en): tagging what language content is in. Prefer locale when region or script variants matter.
language.error: Please use the language code, like en.
language.hint: Two or three small letters, like en
language.label: Language
language.name: language

lei.details: A Legal Entity Identifier: organizations in financial and regulatory contexts. Identity, not routing - prefer bic for payment routing.
lei.error: Please use 20 capital letters and digits, like 5493001KJTIIGC8Y1R12.

attrs.title: Please use 20 capital letters and digits, like 5493001KJTIIGC8Y1R12.

lei.label: Legal Entity ID
lei.name: lei

locale.details: A BCP 47 language tag (en, en-US): a language with optional script and region, for formatting, translations, and user preferences.
locale.error: Please use a language code, like en-US.
locale.label: Language and region
locale.name: locale

mac_address.details: An EUI-48 hardware address: device inventory, DHCP leases. Never an identity for people or accounts - MACs are spoofable and privacy-sensitive.
mac_address.error: Please use six hex pairs with : or -, like 00:1b:44:11:3a:b7.

attrs.title: Please use six hex pairs with : or -, like 00:1b:44:11:3a:b7.

mac_address.label: Hardware address
mac_address.name: mac_address

postgres.note: macaddr is EUI-48; macaddr8 is the EUI-64 variant.

media_range.details: An HTTP media range with wildcards and parameters: Accept-style negotiation. Prefer media_type for one concrete type.
media_range.error: Please use kind/subkind or a *, like text/html;q=0.9.

attrs.title: Please use kind/subkind or a *, like text/html;q=0.9.

media_range.label: Accepted file types
media_range.name: media_range

postgres.note: A range admits wildcards and parameters; media_type admits neither.

media_type.details: A concrete media type like application/json: labeling stored content.
media_type.hint: What kind of file, like application/json

attrs.title: Please write kind/subkind, like application/json.

media_type.label: File type
media_type.name: media_type

object.details: A nested JSON object: structured payloads, settings blobs, documents. Prefer dedicated fields or columns once the shape is stable enough to query.
object.error: Please give named values, like a small card of facts.

html.note: No native JSON input; parse with JSON.parse before submit or use a structured editor.

object.label: Group of fields
object.name: object

postgres.note: json keeps the input text and key order verbatim; jsonb normalizes it and is the indexable one.

orcid.details: An ORCID iD identifying a researcher. Prefer lei for organizations and wikidata_qid for entities outside scholarly identity.
orcid.error: Please use four groups of 4 with dashes, like 0000-0002-1825-0097.

attrs.title: Please use four groups of 4 with dashes, like 0000-0002-1825-0097.

orcid.label: ORCID iD
orcid.name: orcid

phone.details: An E.164 phone number (+country code, digits only): dialing and SMS. Store normalized; display formatting is presentation, not data.
phone.error: Start with + and the country code, no spaces, like +14155552671.
phone.hint: Start with + and your country code

attrs.title: Start with + and the country code, no spaces, like +14155552671.

html.note: Users type local formats; normalize to E.164 before submit (e.g. libphonenumber-js).

phone.label: Phone number
phone.name: phone

port.details: A TCP/UDP port number (0..65535): service endpoints and configuration. Prefer uint16 for 16-bit values that are not ports.
port.error: Please use a whole number from 0 to 65535.
port.label: Port number
port.name: port

postgres.note: No unsigned 16-bit type; integer plus a range check covers 0-65535.

regex.details: An ECMA-262 regular expression source: validation rules and matchers stored as data. Prefer enum when the acceptable values are simply a closed set.
regex.error: That regular expression looks wrong. Try ^[a-z]+$.
regex.label: Text pattern
regex.name: regex

relative_json_pointer.details: A JSON Pointer relative to a known position (1/name). Prefer json_pointer when addressing from the document root.
relative_json_pointer.error: Please start with a number, like 1/name.
relative_json_pointer.hint: Steps up, then a path, like 1/name

attrs.title: Please start with a number, like 1/name.

relative_json_pointer.label: Relative JSON Pointer
relative_json_pointer.name: relative_json_pointer

postgres.note: Resolved against a base pointer; the leading integer counts levels up.

secret.details: Sensitive text that must never be displayed or logged: passwords, API keys. The format is a masking hint, not protection - hash or encrypt at rest.

html.note: Use autocomplete="new-password" or "current-password" for user passwords so password managers engage; "off" for API keys and tokens.

secret.label: Secret
secret.name: secret

postgres.note: The type offers no protection; encrypt with pgcrypto or keep the value out of the database.

secret.standard: OpenAPI Format Registry (display hint only, not a guarantee)

semver.details: A Semantic Version (1.4.2-rc.1): package and API versions with defined precedence. Prefer string for version-ish labels that do not follow SemVer.
semver.error: Please use three numbers with dots, like 1.4.2-rc.1.

attrs.title: Please use three numbers with dots, like 1.4.2-rc.1.

semver.label: Version number
semver.name: semver

postgres.note: Ordering is lexical unless the parts are split out or an extension type is used.

sf_binary.details: An HTTP Structured Fields byte sequence (colon-delimited base64): binary members of structured headers. Prefer base64 outside header serialization.
sf_binary.error: Please wrap base64 in colons, like :aGVsbG8=:.
sf_binary.label: Header bytes
sf_binary.name: sf_binary

postgres.note: Stored decoded; the surrounding colons are Structured Fields syntax, not data.

sf_boolean.details: An HTTP Structured Fields boolean (?1 / ?0): flags in structured headers. Prefer boolean outside header serialization.
sf_boolean.label: Header yes/no
sf_boolean.name: sf_boolean

postgres.note: Serialized as ?1 and ?0 on the wire, which is syntax rather than a distinct type.

sf_decimal.details: An HTTP Structured Fields decimal (three fractional digits): weights and q-values in headers. Prefer decimal outside header serialization.
sf_decimal.error: Please use a number with at most 3 decimals, like 4.5.
sf_decimal.hint: Up to 3 digits after the dot
sf_decimal.label: Header decimal
sf_decimal.name: sf_decimal

postgres.note: At most twelve integer and three fractional digits, which numeric keeps exactly.

sf_integer.details: An HTTP Structured Fields integer (15 digits max): numeric members of structured headers. Prefer int64 outside header serialization.
sf_integer.error: Please use a whole number with up to 15 digits.
sf_integer.label: Header number
sf_integer.name: sf_integer

postgres.note: Structured Fields caps integers at fifteen digits, well inside bigint.

sf_string.details: An HTTP Structured Fields quoted string (printable ASCII): textual members of structured headers. Prefer string outside header serialization.
sf_string.error: Please use plain ASCII characters, like hello world.

attrs.title: Please use plain ASCII characters, like hello world.

sf_string.label: Header text
sf_string.name: sf_string

postgres.note: Printable ASCII only; DQUOTE and backslash are escaped in transport.

sf_token.details: An HTTP Structured Fields token like gzip: short symbolic header values. Prefer enum for closed sets outside HTTP.
sf_token.error: Please start with a letter, no spaces, like gzip.

attrs.title: Please start with a letter, no spaces, like gzip.

sf_token.label: Header token
sf_token.name: sf_token

postgres.note: A bare token, never quoted; that is what distinguishes it from sf_string.

sha256.details: A SHA-256 digest: content addressing, integrity checks, dedup keys. Never for passwords - those take a dedicated password hash stored as secret.

attrs.title: Needs 64 hex characters, like e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855.

html.note: Computed (crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', bytes)), shown read-only.

sha256.label: SHA-256 hash
sha256.name: sha256

postgres.note: 32 decoded bytes; bytea has no fixed-length form, so length is enforced by a check.

slug.details: A lowercase-hyphen URL token (getting-started): readable path segments derived from a title. Presentation identity only - prefer uuid as the real key.
slug.error: Use small letters, digits and single dashes, like getting-started.

attrs.title: Use small letters, digits and single dashes, like getting-started.

html.note: Usually derived from a title: lowercase, NFKD-strip accents, replace runs of non [a-z0-9] with '-', trim '-'.

slug.label: Web address name
slug.name: slug

string.details: Single-line text where a length bound is meaningful: names, titles, labels. Prefer text when there is no maximum, and enum when the values form a closed set.
string.hint: A few words, like a name or a title

html.note: Set maxlength from the length attribute.

string.label: Short text
string.name: string

postgres.note: varchar and text are the same storage; the length is a constraint, not an optimization.

subdivision.details: An ISO 3166-2 subdivision code (US-CA): states, provinces, regions. Carries its country prefix, so no separate country field is needed to interpret it.

attrs.title: Please use country-region, like US-CA.

subdivision.label: State or region
subdivision.name: subdivision

text.details: Unbounded prose: article bodies, comments, logs. Prefer string when a length limit is part of the contract.
text.hint: As many lines as you need
text.label: Long text
text.name: text

time.details: A wall-clock time with an explicit UTC offset. Prefer time_local for schedules that float with the local zone.
time.error: Please add the zone offset, like 14:30:00Z.

html.note: The time input has no offset; append the user's current UTC offset before sending.

time.label: Time with offset
time.name: time

postgres.note: timetz stores a fixed UTC offset, not a zone; plain time drops the offset.

time_local.details: A wall-clock time with no offset: daily schedules like 'every day at 14:30' that follow whatever zone applies. Pair with timezone when the zone is fixed.

html.note: step="1" shows seconds; without it browsers submit HH:MM, which the pattern rejects - append ":00".

time_local.label: Time of day
time_local.name: time_local

postgres.note: Plain time drops the offset, which is exactly what makes it the local variant.

time_local.standard: OpenAPI Format Registry (RFC 3339 partial-time, no offset)

timezone.details: An IANA zone name like America/New_York: user preferences and scheduling context. Store the name, never a raw offset - offsets change with DST and law.
timezone.error: Please pick a time zone, like America/New_York.
timezone.hint: A region and city, like America/New_York
timezone.label: Time zone
timezone.name: timezone

postgres.note: No native zone type; store the IANA name and validate against pg_timezone_names.

uint16.details: Unsigned 16-bit integers (0..65535). Prefer port for network ports specifically, and int32 when a negative value could ever appear.
uint16.error: Please use a whole number from 0 to 65535.
uint16.label: Small count
uint16.name: uint16

postgres.note: No unsigned integers; integer covers the whole uint16 range.

uint32.details: Unsigned 32-bit integers: large counters and IDs from systems that use them. Prefer int64 in new designs; signed types survive arithmetic and language boundaries better.
uint32.error: Please use a whole number from 0 to 4294967295.
uint32.label: Count
uint32.name: uint32

postgres.note: Postgres has no unsigned integers; bigint covers the whole uint32 range.

uint64.details: The full unsigned 64-bit range: hashes and foreign systems' identifiers. Most languages and JSON cannot represent the upper half natively, so values travel as strings; prefer int64 unless the source really uses all 64 bits.

attrs.title: Please use only digits, like 18446744073709551615.

html.note: Not type="number": browsers parse it as a double and lose digits past 2^53. Keep it a string in JS (BigInt for math).

uint64.label: Huge count
uint64.name: uint64

postgres.note: No unsigned 64-bit type; numeric(20, 0) covers the whole uint64 range.

uint8.details: Unsigned bytes (0..255): color channels, small numeric codes. Prefer int32 unless the byte range is intrinsic to the data.
uint8.error: Please use a whole number from 0 to 255.
uint8.label: Tiny count
uint8.name: uint8

postgres.note: Postgres has no unsigned integers; smallint covers the whole uint8 range.

ulid.details: A lexically sortable 128-bit ID in Crockford Base32: time-ordered keys that stay readable as text. Prefer uuid_v7 where native UUID column types and tooling matter.
ulid.error: Please use 26 letters and digits, like 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV.

attrs.title: Please use 26 letters and digits, like 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV.

html.note: Generated, shown read-only.

ulid.label: Sortable ID
ulid.name: ulid

postgres.note: 128-bit like a UUID; storable as uuid if the Crockford base32 form is converted on the way in.

unix_time.details: Seconds since the Unix epoch as an integer: compact machine timestamps and TTLs. Prefer date_time for anything humans or APIs read directly.
unix_time.error: Please use whole seconds since 1970, like 1786000000.

html.note: Show as a local date-time and convert: Math.floor(new Date(value).getTime() / 1000).

unix_time.label: Unix timestamp
unix_time.name: unix_time
unix_time.standard: POSIX.1-2024 (IEEE Std 1003.1-2024) seconds since the Epoch

uri.details: An absolute URI with scheme: links, webhooks, resource locators. Use string for relative paths.
uri.error: That link looks wrong. Try https://example.com/page.
uri.label: Web link
uri.name: uri

uri_reference.details: A URI reference, absolute or relative: redirect targets, in-site paths. Prefer uri when an absolute, scheme-carrying value is required.
uri_reference.error: That link or path looks wrong. Try /a/b?c=1.
uri_reference.hint: A full link or a path like /a/b
uri_reference.label: Link or path
uri_reference.name: uri_reference

uri_template.details: An RFC 6570 URL pattern with {variables}: route and link templates. Prefer uri for concrete, already-expanded links.
uri_template.label: Link template
uri_template.name: uri_template

uuid.details: A 128-bit universal identifier, any version: primary keys and references. Which version to mint (such as time-ordered v7) is a generation option, not a separate type.
uuid.error: That ID looks wrong. It should look like f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6.
uuid.hint: A long ID with dashes, made by the computer

attrs.title: That ID looks wrong. It should look like f81d4fae-7dec-11d0-a765-00a0c91e6bf6.

html.note: Usually generated (crypto.randomUUID()) and shown read-only rather than typed.

uuid.label: Unique ID
uuid.name: uuid

postgres.note: Stored as 16 bytes regardless of the input spelling.

uuid_v7.details: A time-ordered UUID: new primary keys that index and sort by creation time. Prefer uuid when accepting identifiers you did not mint.
uuid_v7.error: It needs a 7 after the second dash, like 018f4b2c-9c1e-7a3b-8f2d-1a2b3c4d5e6f.
uuid_v7.hint: A unique ID that sorts by time

attrs.title: It needs a 7 after the second dash, like 018f4b2c-9c1e-7a3b-8f2d-1a2b3c4d5e6f.

html.note: Generated server-side, shown read-only.

uuid_v7.label: Time-ordered ID
uuid_v7.name: uuid_v7

postgres.note: Same storage as any UUID; the time ordering is a property of the value, not the type.

wikidata_qid.details: A Wikidata entity ID (Q42): linking records to globally known entities. Prefer the domain registry when one exists - doi, orcid, lei, isbn.
wikidata_qid.error: Please use Q and a number, like Q42.
wikidata_qid.hint: Q and a number, like Q42

attrs.title: Please use Q and a number, like Q42.

wikidata_qid.label: Wikidata ID
wikidata_qid.name: wikidata_qid
